system_description.narrative_title: Houthi Attacks on Saudi Airports Spur Regional Escalation and Energy/Aviation Shock
system_description.narrative_summary: A concentrated wave of Houthi strikes against Saudi airports and energy assets is driving a rapid escalation in the Iran–Saudi confrontation, pulling in regional states and raising the risk of wider military and economic fallout. The system is open: kinetic attacks, diplomatic signaling, airline and corporate responses, and commodity-market reactions circulate feedbacks that amplify disruption to aviation, oil shipments, conferences, and investor sentiment. Policy, military, and market responses (airline cancellations, executive pullouts, strikes, convoy interdictions) in turn affect the incentives for further attacks or de-escalation.
system_description.scope: Actors, processes and assets directly involved in and immediately affected by the strikes and their fallout — Houthi militias, Saudi security and infrastructure (airports, Aramco sites), Iranian influence and regional proxies, Gulf shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, international airlines and aviation safety authorities, energy companies and commodity markets, major conferences and summit diplomacy.
system_description.super_system: Global geopolitical–energy–financial system (international security and global commodity markets)
adjacent_subsystems: Regional diplomatic and security architectures (GCC, Iran, US, allied responses)
Global financial markets and commodity trading

variables.name: Kinetic attack rate
variables.description: The frequency per unit time of kinetic strikes (missiles, drones, ballistic weapons) directed at civil or energy infrastructure in the region.

variables.name: Strike hit rate
variables.description: The proportion of launched attacks that successfully impact intended infrastructure or assets.

variables.name: Critical infrastructure operational capacity
variables.description: The aggregated share of airports, terminals, refineries and other key energy/transport facilities functioning at designed capacity.

variables.name: Air route connectivity
variables.description: The degree of scheduled passenger and cargo route connectivity and available seat/cargo capacity between the region and global networks.

variables.name: Maritime transit throughput
variables.description: The volume and rate of commercial shipping transits through regional chokepoints and nearby sea lanes.

variables.name: Energy export flow
variables.description: The continuous rate of hydrocarbon (oil and LNG) shipments leaving the region toward global markets.

variables.name: Commodity price volatility
variables.description: The measured volatility of regional-relevant commodity prices (crude, diesel, gas, jet fuel) over short- to medium-term horizons.

variables.name: Investor risk sentiment
variables.description: The market perception of geopolitical and economic risk driving capital allocation, risk premia and asset re-pricing for the region.

variables.name: Airline cancellation and reroute rate
variables.description: The rate at which commercial carriers cancel, suspend, or reroute scheduled flights in response to security and operational conditions.

variables.name: Insurance premium level
variables.description: The prevailing cost level of war/terrorism and marine/aviation insurance for operations in and transiting the region.

variables.name: Diplomatic engagement intensity
variables.description: The frequency and intensity of diplomatic communications, negotiations, and crisis-management activity among regional and external actors.

variables.name: Military response intensity
variables.description: The scale and tempo of kinetic countermeasures, strikes, patrols and interdictions deployed in response to attacks.

variables.name: Proxy network capacity
variables.description: The operational capability, logistical reach and command influence of irregular or proxy actor networks operating in the theatre.

variables.name: Public travel safety perception
variables.description: The prevailing public and traveler perception of safety for regional air travel and maritime transit.

variables.name: Conference and event participation rate
variables.description: The rate at which planned conferences, summits and corporate events proceed with expected attendance levels in the region.

variables.name: Supply chain delay level
variables.description: The average additional transit and processing time experienced by goods and passengers due to regional disruptions.

catalysts.title: Sustained Houthi missile/drone campaign
catalysts.description: Houthis continue targeting Saudi airports, energy sites and shipping with missiles/drones, producing a sustained campaign of strikes and warnings. Likely to persist while tit-for-tat strikes and rhetoric continue.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines: 'Houthis attack Riyadh airport', 'Houthis show military reach', 'Houthis step up attacks'.

catalysts.title: Extended Riyadh airport closure / suspension
catalysts.description: Riyadh's airport remains closed or partially closed and airlines extend cancellations, constraining passenger and cargo flows in the near term.
catalysts.rationale: 'Saudi capital's airport to remain shut this week' and 'Airlines cancel flights to Saudi Arabia after Riyadh airport attacks'.

catalysts.title: Energy summit cancellations / executive withdrawals
catalysts.description: Senior energy executives and companies withdraw or scale back attendance at Riyadh energy events, reducing participation and signalling market and political concern.
catalysts.rationale: 'BP not able to attend Riyadh energy conference' and 'Oil chiefs pull out of Riyadh energy congress'.

catalysts.title: U.S./coalition military escalation
catalysts.description: Political and military moves by the U.S. or partners to join or intensify operations alongside Saudi responses could broaden the campaign and provoke counter-actions.
catalysts.rationale: 'Trump says he is going to look at joining Saudi Arabia' and 'US hits commercial tanker in Gulf of Oman'.

catalysts.title: Further strikes on Aramco / energy facilities
catalysts.description: Additional attacks targeting Aramco buildings or other energy infrastructure risk operations disruptions and shipping slowdowns if repeated or successful.
catalysts.rationale: 'Saudi Aramco HQ attacked', 'Loud booms heard near Saudi Aramco headquarters'.

catalysts.title: Deferred US–Saudi nonstop route launches (by March)
catalysts.description: U.S. carriers delay planned new nonstop services to Saudi Arabia (e.g., Delta) until March, reducing near-term connectivity and signalling prolonged disruption.
catalysts.rationale: 'Delta delays debut of Saudi Arabia service until March' and 'FAA warns U.S. airlines of safety risks'.

catalysts.title: War/marine/aviation insurance premium spike
catalysts.description: Rising attacks, tanker incidents and longer voyages drive up war, marine and aviation insurance costs, raising transport costs and rerouting decisions.
catalysts.rationale: 'Oil Tanker Rates Surge Amid Rising Attacks' and 'tanker attacks, longer voyages' headlines.

catalysts.title: Regulatory advisories escalate to flight bans
catalysts.description: Aviation authorities (FAA, others) may broaden warnings or restrictions, prompting carriers to suspend routes and raising cancellation levels.
catalysts.rationale: 'FAA tells U.S. airlines to exercise caution' and 'Airlines cancel flights to Saudi Arabia after Riyadh airport attacks'.
